The subsequent segments discuss Mary Shelley's novel Frankenstein, highlighting its central themes of creation and creator responsibility.

When interpreting these themes through diverse reader perspectives, the text suggests two distinct lenses. For readers with backgrounds in science and ethics, the narrative serves as an early critique of scientific hubris, emphasizing the moral obligations that accompany technological or biological advancement. Conversely, readers with religious perspectives may view the story as a cautionary tale regarding the transgression of divine boundaries, specifically the act of "playing God." This dual interpretation underscores how a single literary work can resonate differently depending on the cultural, professional, and philosophical background of the audience.
